78% Of German Electricity Came From Renewables On July 25
Obviously Germany doesn't have the big oil producer lobby in their national legislature to pay politicians to kill renewable energy initiatives.

Oil doesn't usually power electric grids, which is what the German stat is referring to. In the US, that's coal and natural gas. Also, renewable energy receives plenty of corporate handouts in the US, just like fossil fuel industries. The issue isn't evil fossil fuels beating down the white knights of renewable energy. We would have tons of renewable infrastructure to build, plus fossil fuels are cheap enough to be marketable. In the short run and the foreseeable long run (obviously not indefinitely, but for a long time), fossil fuels are a viable fuel source.

Concerning the lobbies, the problem isn't big industry, it's big government. When you have a massive federal government that dishes out billions upon billions of taxpayer dollars and legislative benefits to whomever gives the best campaign donations, you're going to breed crony capitalism. Industries are behaving just like any rational actor in a market does -- they're self interested. We should never expect businesses to behave ethically. Instead, we should expect the government that we have direct control over to make the good moral choices and let the amoral corporations adjust to the parameters we set. In this case, that parameter is the size of government itself. Any time a corporation does behave ethically, which they sometimes do, consider that fickle human kindness and not a benchmark for how economics should work.

Return power to the states and you'll immediately see less incentive for corporations to spend such huge amounts of money on lobbying. States have less funding and less scope in their legislative jurisdiction. There is simply less for a corporation to gain from lobbying a state. Of course they will still lobby, as they should have the right to, but the negative effects will be mitigated. Additionally, grassroots lobbying is a lot easier at the state level than at the federal level, so the "common man" is on more equal footing in this kind of government.

What can we do as individuals, aside from voting in politicians who want to return to good ol' fashioned Madisonian Federalism? Go off the grid either on your own or through the formation of cooperatives (say, in your neighborhood or a few neighborhoods). The Tesla home battery might make this a viable option soon enough, which is very exciting.

Bear in mind that electricity represents only a fraction of energy consumption, that is, it doesn't take into account all the cars, trucks, homes, factories, etc. that run on oil, gas or coal. Renewables in Germany account for less than 10% of primary energy consumption. So it's good news, but it doesn't mean that windmills and solar are providing all of Germany's energy needs. Not by a long shot.

German electricity is also 3 times more expensive than in the US. It is second only to Denmark in the developed world. Can you honestly pay 3 times for more for your power bill? And that is just the beginning. Your employer is going to pay 3 times more too. You'll need that $15/hr job just to pay for your $9 burger.

People forget that just because Greece is teetering on the brink as a failed nation that doesn't mean Germany is actually healthy. Their economy is just as unsustainable.
